description: Build a ROP chain. target must be "linux-execve" (ELF x86/x64 only, ported from ROPgadget's ropmaker: x86 int 0x80 / x64 syscall, "/bin//sh" written to a writable section) or "windows-virtualprotect". Returns the chain IR as JSON (words with kinds gadget_addr / immediate / data_addr / code_addr / padding plus the referenced gadget table, each entry carrying the same stable id find_gadgets returns), the equivalent python exploit script, arch, description and word_count. A binary that lacks a required gadget fails with not_found. Chain builds bypass the gadget cache.

api_addr.description:
windows-virtualprotect: runtime address of the API (hex). Primary
resolution path; without it the PE must import the API (IAT).

arch.description:
Architecture slice for a fat (Universal) Mach-O, e.g. "x86_64",
"arm64", "i386". REQUIRED for a multi-slice container: without it
the scan is refused rather than concatenating slices whose virtual
address ranges overlap (CORE-03).

badbytes.description:
Reject chain words whose packed value contains these bytes
(e.g. "0a|0d" or "00-1f").

base.description: Rebase the image base at load time (hex string, e.g. "0x400000").

binary_path.description:
Absolute path to the binary; must be inside one of the server's
allow_roots (get_server_config lists them).

cfg_aware.description: CFG/CET-aware scan: keep only endbr64/endbr32-entering gadgets.

offset.description: Offset added to gadget and data-section addresses (hex string).

shellcode_addr.description:
windows-virtualprotect: runtime shellcode address (hex; default:
the binary's writable .data section).

name: build_rop_chain

id.description:
The same stable id `find_gadgets` returns, so an agent can look the
gadget up with `get_gadgets`. `null` when the chain's scan no longer
holds the gadget's bytes.

source_gadget.description:
Index into `chain.gadgets` for a `gadget_addr` word; `null`
otherwise. It used to be omitted rather than null.

value.description: Hex, so a 64-bit word survives a JSON parser with 53-bit numbers.

Warning.description:
A non-fatal fact the agent has to know to read the result correctly
(CRIT-03 item 4).

`fallback_section_names` used to be a bare boolean with no explanation,
and truncation was announced nowhere at all. Every entry has a stable
`code` to branch on and a `message` to show a human.

detail.description: Free-form detail (the slice name, the architecture, …).

field.description: The response field the warning is about, when it is about one.

description: Find ROP gadgets in a binary (ret-terminated). Results are RANKED by default (order="rank": usability tier, then quality, then fewest instructions, then fewest side effects, then address), so the first page is the useful gadgets rather than the alphabetical head; order="address"|"quality"|"text" are also accepted. Every record carries a stable id, the classification (class, labels, regs_written, regs_read, regs_from_stack, side_effects, terminator, usability) and delay_slot. Filter server-side with class/label/writes_reg/reads_reg/preserves_regs/from_stack/terminator/max_side_effects/max_insns instead of pulling gadgets into context. Page with next_cursor. binary_path must be an absolute path inside one of the server's allow_roots (call get_server_config to list them); anything else returns path_denied. depth above max_depth is rejected, not clamped. A request that exceeds timeout_secs is STOPPED, not orphaned, and notifications/cancelled stops it too.

arch.description:
Architecture slice for a fat (Universal) Mach-O, e.g. "x86_64",
"arm64", "i386". REQUIRED for a multi-slice container: without it
the scan is refused rather than concatenating slices whose virtual
address ranges overlap (CORE-03).

badbytes.description:
Reject gadgets whose final address contains these bytes
(e.g. "0a|0d" or "00-1f").

base.description:
Rebase the image base at load time (hex string, e.g. "0x400000";
"0" for RVA-style addresses).

binary_path.description:
Absolute path to the binary; must be inside one of the server's
allow_roots (get_server_config lists them).

class.description:
Keep only gadgets whose primary class is one of these
(comma-separated): reg-write, stack-pivot, mem-read, mem-write,
arithmetic, syscall, dispatcher, other.

cursor.description:
`next_cursor` from a previous page of THIS query. Re-send every
other parameter unchanged; `max_results` and `timeout_secs` may
change. A cursor from a different query returns `cursor_expired`.

from_stack.description:
Require the `writes_reg` registers to be loaded off the STACK (a
pop, or a stack-based load), which is what makes them controllable
from the chain payload. With no `writes_reg`, requires at least one
stack-loaded register.

label.description:
Keep only gadgets carrying at least one of these labels (same
vocabulary as `class`; a gadget can earn several).

max_insns.description: Keep only gadgets with at most this many instructions.

max_results.description: Maximum gadgets returned per page (default 1000, hard max 50000).

max_side_effects.description: Keep only gadgets with at most this many side effects.

offset.description: Offset added to gadget addresses after any rebase (hex string).

only.description: Keep only gadgets containing these instructions (e.g. "pop|ret").

order.description:
Result ordering, applied BEFORE paging. "rank" (the default) is
usability tier, then quality, then fewest instructions, then fewest
side effects, then address — it is what puts `pop rdi ; ret` at the
top instead of `adc al, 0x89 ; retf 0xc281`. Also "address",
"quality" and "text" (the pre-0.3 default). Anything else is
rejected with the valid set in the error.

preserves_regs.description:
Keep only gadgets that write NONE of these registers — "do not
clobber rsi or rdx".

reads_reg.description: Keep only gadgets that read ALL of these registers.

section.description:
Executable section name(s) to scan; comma-separated, `*` globbing
(e.g. ".text" or ".init*,.plt").

sort_by.description:
Deprecated alias for `order`, kept because it used to be the only
way to ask for anything but traversal order. Ignored when `order`
is given.

terminator.description:
Keep only gadgets with this terminator kind: "ret" (every returning
form), "jmp", "call", "syscall", "none", or "any".

writes_reg.description:
Keep only gadgets that write ALL of these registers
(comma-separated, e.g. "rdi"). Names are matched lowercase and
without a `$`/`%` sigil.

name: find_gadgets

GadgetRecord.description:
One gadget, in the shape every gadget-returning tool emits.

Invariant: the field set does not depend on the request. A gadget from a
scan with no `section` parameter carries `"section": null`, not a missing
key; an x86-64 ELF carries `"arch": null` and `"delay_slot": false`, not
nothing at all. `tests/schema_conformance.rs` asserts the four shapes
that used to differ — plain, `section=.text`, MIPS, and the fat Mach-O —
have identical key sets.

arch.description:
Fat Mach-O slice this gadget came from; `null` for every other
container.

class.description:
Primary class (`reg-write`, `stack-pivot`, `mem-read`, `mem-write`,
`arithmetic`, `syscall`, `dispatcher`, `other`); `null` when the
architecture has no classifier.

delay_slot.description:
MIPS/SPARC: the LAST instruction is the branch's delay slot, so it
executes **before** control transfers. `rf_scan` has always computed
this and every output boundary dropped it.

id.description:
Stable identity: `g_` + base32 of the first 10 bytes of
`blake3(binary_sha256 || vaddr_le || bytes)`. Independent of every
scan parameter, so the same gadget has the same id across calls,
processes and cache evictions. Pass a list of these to
`get_gadgets`.

labels.description: Every class the gadget earns, not just the primary one.

low_confidence.description:
The classification came from disassembly text rather than decoder
metadata, so treat the semantic fields as advisory.

privileged.description:
Contains a privileged or undefined instruction, so it faults in user
mode and cannot appear in a chain.

quality.description: TAXONOMY.md R12 quality score, higher is cleaner.

regs_from_stack.description:
The subset of `regs_written` loaded off the stack — the registers a
chain payload can actually control.

regs_written.description: Registers the gadget writes, lowercase and sigil-free.

section.description:
Section containing the gadget; `null` when no `section` filter was
applied (the scan then has no section table to consult).

side_effects.description: Instructions that earn at least one label.

stack_delta.description:
Net change to the stack pointer. **Always `null` in v0.3**: the
computation is ECO-07/CLS-09 and lands in v0.4. The field is here
now so the record shape does not change when it does.

terminator.description:
How the gadget hands control on: `ret`, `ret-imm`, `retf`, `iret`,
`far`, `jmp`, `call`, `syscall`, `none`.

vaddr.description:
Zero-padded hex address, for humans. The padding width is 8 on a
32-bit target and 16 on a 64-bit one, which is why `vaddr_u64`
exists.

vaddr_u64.description:
The same address as a number. Agents doing arithmetic should use
this and never parse `vaddr`.

Warning.description:

detail.description: Free-form detail (the slice name, the architecture, …).

field.description: The response field the warning is about, when it is about one.

binary_label.description:
The binary's path relative to its allow root — what the audit log
records, and never the caller's spelling of the path.

cache.description:
`hit` when the gadget set came from a cache (in memory, pinned for
a cursor, or authenticated from disk), `miss` when it was scanned.

cache_key.description: Key of the cached scan; the second path component of `resource_uri`.

fallback_section_names.description:
The binary has no section names and synthetic `PT_LOAD#n` names were
matched instead. Also reported in `warnings`.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque token for the next page; `null` on the last one. Send it back
as `cursor` with the SAME query parameters.

offset.description: Index of this page's first gadget within the ordered result.

order.description:
The order actually applied: `rank`, `address`, `quality`, `text` or
`ids`. Echoed because the default changed to `rank` and an agent
must not have to assume.

resource_uri.description:
`ropfinder://scan/<cache_key>/gadgets.ndjson` — the WHOLE ordered

Present only when the result was paged.

total_count.description: Gadgets matching the query, before paging.

warnings.description: Non-fatal facts. Always present; `[]` when there are none.

workspace_file.description:
The same NDJSON as a real file, when the server was started with
`--workspace-dir`. An agent with filesystem tools should grep this
instead of paging.

description: Get binary metadata as JSON: format, arch, endianness, addr_size, image_base, entry, sections (name/vaddr/size/executable/writable), PE imports (iat_vaddr is the IAT slot the loader patches; hint_name_vaddr is the IMAGE_IMPORT_BY_NAME record), fat Mach-O slices, binary_sha256 and warnings. The shape is fixed: an ELF reports slices: [] and a fat Mach-O reports sections: []. No scan is performed. Bounded like every other tool: timeout_secs (default 60), --max-file-bytes, and max_sections/max_imports (default 4096 each) — a truncated array is announced in warnings, never silently short.

base.description: Rebase the image base before reporting addresses (hex string).

binary_path.description:
Absolute path to the binary; must be inside one of the server's
allow_roots (get_server_config lists them).

max_imports.description:
Maximum imports reported (default 4096). A larger array is
truncated and `warnings` carries `imports_truncated`.

max_sections.description:
Maximum sections reported (default 4096). A larger array is
truncated and `warnings` carries `sections_truncated`.

name: get_binary_info

description: Resolve stable gadget ids (the `id` field of any gadget record, e.g. "g_ab12cd34ef56gh78") back to full records, so a plan can name gadgets instead of re-sending their text. Rescans the binary at `depth` (default 10) and matches by id; an id is independent of every scan parameter except `base`, so pass the same `base` the ids came from. Ids that do not resolve are reported in warnings.ids_not_found rather than failing the call. Results are returned in the order the ids were given.

arch.description: Architecture slice for a fat (Universal) Mach-O.

base.description:
Rebase the image base at load time (hex string). Must match the
scan the ids came from: an id is independent of every scan
parameter EXCEPT `base`, which relabels the whole address space.

binary_path.description:
Absolute path to the binary; must be inside one of the server's
allow_roots (get_server_config lists them).

depth.description:
Search depth the ids were found at (default 10). An id from a
depth-10 scan will not resolve in a depth-4 one.

ids.description:
Stable gadget ids, as returned in `gadgets[].id` (e.g.
"g_ab12cd34ef56gh78"). Ids that do not resolve are reported in
`warnings` rather than failing the call.

offset.description: Offset added to gadget addresses after any rebase (hex string).

name: get_gadgets

GadgetRecord.description:
One gadget, in the shape every gadget-returning tool emits.

Invariant: the field set does not depend on the request. A gadget from a
scan with no `section` parameter carries `"section": null`, not a missing
key; an x86-64 ELF carries `"arch": null` and `"delay_slot": false`, not
nothing at all. `tests/schema_conformance.rs` asserts the four shapes
that used to differ — plain, `section=.text`, MIPS, and the fat Mach-O —
have identical key sets.

arch.description:
Fat Mach-O slice this gadget came from; `null` for every other
container.

class.description:
Primary class (`reg-write`, `stack-pivot`, `mem-read`, `mem-write`,
`arithmetic`, `syscall`, `dispatcher`, `other`); `null` when the
architecture has no classifier.

delay_slot.description:
MIPS/SPARC: the LAST instruction is the branch's delay slot, so it
executes **before** control transfers. `rf_scan` has always computed
this and every output boundary dropped it.

id.description:
Stable identity: `g_` + base32 of the first 10 bytes of
`blake3(binary_sha256 || vaddr_le || bytes)`. Independent of every
scan parameter, so the same gadget has the same id across calls,
processes and cache evictions. Pass a list of these to
`get_gadgets`.

labels.description: Every class the gadget earns, not just the primary one.

low_confidence.description:
The classification came from disassembly text rather than decoder
metadata, so treat the semantic fields as advisory.

privileged.description:
Contains a privileged or undefined instruction, so it faults in user
mode and cannot appear in a chain.

quality.description: TAXONOMY.md R12 quality score, higher is cleaner.

regs_from_stack.description:
The subset of `regs_written` loaded off the stack — the registers a
chain payload can actually control.

regs_written.description: Registers the gadget writes, lowercase and sigil-free.

section.description:
Section containing the gadget; `null` when no `section` filter was
applied (the scan then has no section table to consult).

side_effects.description: Instructions that earn at least one label.

stack_delta.description:
Net change to the stack pointer. **Always `null` in v0.3**: the
computation is ECO-07/CLS-09 and lands in v0.4. The field is here
now so the record shape does not change when it does.

terminator.description:
How the gadget hands control on: `ret`, `ret-imm`, `retf`, `iret`,
`far`, `jmp`, `call`, `syscall`, `none`.

vaddr.description:
Zero-padded hex address, for humans. The padding width is 8 on a
32-bit target and 16 on a 64-bit one, which is why `vaddr_u64`
exists.

vaddr_u64.description:
The same address as a number. Agents doing arithmetic should use
this and never parse `vaddr`.

Warning.description:
A non-fatal fact the agent has to know to read the result correctly
(CRIT-03 item 4).

`fallback_section_names` used to be a bare boolean with no explanation,
and truncation was announced nowhere at all. Every entry has a stable
`code` to branch on and a `message` to show a human.

detail.description: Free-form detail (the slice name, the architecture, …).

field.description: The response field the warning is about, when it is about one.

binary_label.description:
The binary's path relative to its allow root — what the audit log
records, and never the caller's spelling of the path.

cache.description:
`hit` when the gadget set came from a cache (in memory, pinned for
a cursor, or authenticated from disk), `miss` when it was scanned.

cache_key.description: Key of the cached scan; the second path component of `resource_uri`.

fallback_section_names.description:
The binary has no section names and synthetic `PT_LOAD#n` names were
matched instead. Also reported in `warnings`.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque token for the next page; `null` on the last one. Send it back
as `cursor` with the SAME query parameters.

offset.description: Index of this page's first gadget within the ordered result.

order.description:
The order actually applied: `rank`, `address`, `quality`, `text` or
`ids`. Echoed because the default changed to `rank` and an agent
must not have to assume.

resource_uri.description:
`ropfinder://scan/<cache_key>/gadgets.ndjson` — the WHOLE ordered
result, one `GadgetRecord` per line, readable with `resources/read`.
Present only when the result was paged.

total_count.description: Gadgets matching the query, before paging.

warnings.description: Non-fatal facts. Always present; `[]` when there are none.

workspace_file.description:
The same NDJSON as a real file, when the server was started with
`--workspace-dir`. An agent with filesystem tools should grep this
instead of paging.

description: Report the server's effective configuration: allow_roots (the only directories binary_path may name), max_depth, max_file_bytes, max_results, max_concurrent, scan_threads, max_gadgets, timeout_secs, cursor_ttl_secs, whether an on-disk cache and a workspace directory are enabled, the complete list of `order` values, the complete list of error codes, and the server version. Call this first: paths outside allow_roots are refused with a single path_denied code that deliberately reveals nothing about the target, and a run of refusals is treated as filesystem probing.
name: get_server_config

error_codes.description: Every code an error can carry.

description: Report this session's counters: requests_total and requests_by_tool, ok/denied/timeout/cancelled/error totals, denied_consecutive and probing_suspected (a run of path_denied results is the signal that an agent is enumerating the filesystem), wedged_total (workers that did not stop within 5 s of being cancelled), busy_total, inflight, bytes_read_total, and the cache's hit/miss/eviction/tamper counters with its live cache_bytes against cache_mem_max_bytes.
name: get_server_stats

cache.description:
The cache counters, as `crate::cache::Cache::stats_json` renders
them. Left as a free-form object so the cache's own counters can
grow without a schema change.

description: Run a ROPgadget-style scan with explicit flags. args is a list like ["--depth", "6", "--only", "pop|ret"]. Allowlist: --depth --norop --nojop --nosys --only --filter --re --range --section --base --offset --badbytes --align --multibr --json --arch --all --callPreceded; anything else (--string, --dump, --console, ...) is rejected. --align is ROPgadget's real scan-time alignment (decimal, as in ROPgadget's argparse; write 0x.. only if you mean hex), not an address post-filter. --arch names a fat Mach-O slice and is REQUIRED for a multi-slice binary. The result is ordered, filtered and paged exactly like find_gadgets.

args.description:
ROPgadget-style flags, e.g. ["--depth", "6", "--only", "pop|ret"].
Restricted to the allowlist: --depth --norop --nojop --nosys --only
--filter --re --range --section --base --offset --badbytes --align
--multibr --json. Anything else is rejected.

binary_path.description:
Absolute path to the binary; must be inside one of the server's
allow_roots (get_server_config lists them).

class.description: Keep only gadgets whose primary class is one of these.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` from a previous page of THIS query.

from_stack.description: Require the `writes_reg` registers to come off the stack.

label.description: Keep only gadgets carrying at least one of these labels.

max_results.description: Maximum gadgets returned per page (default 1000, hard max 50000).

preserves_regs.description: Keep only gadgets that write NONE of these registers.

reads_reg.description: Keep only gadgets that read ALL of these registers.

writes_reg.description: Keep only gadgets that write ALL of these registers.
